# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Report: `/app` — Transaction Enrichment / Categorization Service

## 1. Overall Codebase Structure

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                       # python:3.9.2 base; runs gunicorn on port 9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                     # setuptools; Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, sklearn, scipy
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py              # Flask app factory + request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py            # 936 lines; Flask routes; per-bank dispatch pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/             # 35 bank-specific categorizer modules (Andhra, Axis, BOB,
        │                            #  BOI, Bandhan, BOM, Canara, Central, Citi, CityUnion, DCB,
        │                            #  Federal, HDFC, ICICI, IDBI, IDFC, Indian, Indusind,
        │                            #  Karnataka, KarurVyasa, Kotak, PNB, Paytm, RBL, SBI, SVC,
        │                            #  Saraswat, SouthIndian, StandardCharted, Syndicate,
        │                            #  TamilnadMerchantile, UCO, UnionBank, YES, AuSmallFinanceBank)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py                   # tokenizer helpers (sep_by_dash, py_extract, fuzzy_match)
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py        # 432 lines of bank-specific regex constants
            ├── RegexConstants.py            # cross-bank merchant/category regexes
            ├── CleanName.py                 # 1971 lines; merchant name normalization
            ├── CardCleanNames.py / CardPurpose.py   # credit-card variants
            ├── Purpose.py                   # subcategory ("purpose") assignment
            ├── InternalPayment.py           # self-transfer detection via fuzzy name match
            ├── SalaryDetection.py, RecurrentTxns.py, PFMCategorization.py,
            ├── SimpleDescription.py
            └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py / TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

- **Language:** Pure Python 3.9 (pandas-vectorized regex rules; no ML at inference — despite sklearn in deps).
- **Framework:** Flask app served by gunicorn (`Dockerfile`, `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py:7`).
- **Build tooling:** `pip3 install -e .` via `setup.py` (`/app/categorizationapp/setup.py`). No Makefile, no CI config.
- **Architecture:** `POST /categorizeTransaction` (`Controller.py:69-70`) normalizes a JSON transaction list into a DataFrame, then dispatches on `bank` to `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(...)`, followed by a shared pipeline: `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` → optional `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`. Each bank script builds `conditions_choices` lists and applies them with `np.select(...)` to populate `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, `partyName`, `party2`.

## 2. Where Enrichment/Categorization Logic Lives

- **Category derivation (`transactionCategory`):** each `BankScripts/<Bank>.py`, first `np.select` block (e.g. `HDFC.py:11-104`, `SBI.py:10-70`, `ICICI.py:9-90`, `Kotak.py:~10-72`). Default category is `"TRANSFER"`.
- **Counterparty name (`partyName`):** later `np.select` blocks in the same bank scripts, using helpers from `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` (`sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_`, `sep_by_colon`, `py_extract` at `AppUtil.py:14-66`) and regex constants from `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`.
- **Merchant name normalization:** `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9` (`clean_names`) — ~1900 lines mapping raw partyName/description to canonical merchant names.
- **Subcategory/purpose:** `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9` (`purpose`) using regexes in `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`.
- **Category enums:** `UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (e.g. line 57 `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT="Cheque"`, line 83 `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"`).

## 3. Test Fixtures / Labelled Corpus / Test Command

**None exist in this repository.** Verified exhaustively:
- `git ls-files` shows only the 55 source files above — no `tests/`, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, `Makefile`, `.github/`, or CSV/JSON fixture files anywhere.
- `.gitignore` ignores `*.csv` and `TEST*.xml`, which suggests labelled statement CSVs and unit-test reports existed in the original developers' workflow but were deliberately excluded from version control.
- There is **no test command**; `setup.py` declares no test dependencies. The only executable entry points are the Flask app (`gunicorn ... categorizationapp:app` in the Dockerfile) or hitting `POST /categorizeTransaction` manually.

## 4. Specific Files/Functions for the Requested Logic

All category/name logic is inside the single `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` function of each bank script (there are no smaller named functions; rules are entries in `conditions_choices` lists).

### 4a. Cheque categorization (CHEQUE_DEPOSIT / CHEQUE_PAID)

| File | Lines | Snippet |
|---|---|---|
| `BankScripts/HDFC.py` | 71, 73-75, 100 | `"\\b[Cc][Hh][Qq]\\b|^I/W CHQ RETURN|[Cc]heque|CHEQUE"` + `type.eq("CREDIT")` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; line 100: 16-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` |
| `BankScripts/Kotak.py` | 64-67 | `"\\bCLG\\b|\\bMICR\\b|\\bCHQ\\b|^BY INST |^TRF CHQ[0-9]"` CREDIT → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; DEBIT → `CHEQUE_PAID`; remark `^[0-9]{3,5}$` fallback |
| `BankScripts/SBI.py` | 44-47 | `"\\bCLG\\b|^BY CLEARING|^TO CLEARING|\\bCHQ\\b|CHEQUE|CHEQ NO"` DEBIT→`CHEQUE_PAID`, CREDIT→`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; `\\bCH [0-9]{6}-` |
| `BankScripts/ICICI.py` | 69-72 | `\\bC[Ll][Gg]\\b|INWARD CLEARING`; also remark-based `CHEQUE` match |
| `BankScripts/Axis.py` | 56-59 | `\\bC[Ll][Gg]\\b` + remark `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (bare cheque number in reference) |
| `BankScripts/BOB.py` | 68-69 | includes `MICR INWD CLG|\\bBY\\b INST\\b|^SER[A-Z]{3}-|^B[yY] [A-Z]` |
| `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py` | 65, 74 | `CHEQUE DEPOSIT|\\bCHQ NO|...|MICR CLG|BY CLG TRF|^CLEARING...` |
| Other banks | PNB.py:58,61; YES.py:45,53; UCO.py:37,45; UnionBank.py:51; Federal.py:42; Canara.py:70; Central.py:46; CityUnion.py:41; Indian.py:40; IDFC.py:42; IDBI.py:57-58; Indusind.py:57; Karnataka.py:45; KarurVyasa.py:49,51; RBL.py:48-49; Saraswat.py:39; SouthIndian.py:33; StandardCharted.py:45; Syndicate.py:53; TamilnadMerchantile.py:34; Bandhan.py:35; BOI.py:40; Andhra.py:47; AuSmallFinanceBank.py:39; Citi.py:66 | Same pattern family (`CLG`, `CHQ`, `CHEQUE`, `BY INST`, numeric-remark heuristics) |

Cheque returns/penalties: e.g. `HDFC.py:30,69-72`, `Citi.py:30` (`CHEQUE RETURNED|RETURN OF MICR CLG CHQ|CHQ. RTN`), `BankRegexConstants.py:341-342,370,374,386,392,404`.

### 4b. Cheque counterparty-name extraction

- **HDFC** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:187-197` ("#cheque" block), driven by `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` defined in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py:81-90`:
  ```python
  [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("CHEQUE_DEPOSIT") & transactions.description.str.contains(HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1, ...), sep_by_colon(transactions.description,1,2)],
  ...
  [transactions.description.str.contains(HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN10, ...), py_extract(transactions.description, pat=HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN10, index=0)],
  ```
  e.g. `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN10 = "CHQ DEP - .* - MICR.*:(.*):"` (BankRegexConstants.py:90). Later cleanup: `HDFC.py:260` blanks names matching `"Micr Clg|Chq Paid"`.
- **PNB** — `BankScripts/PNB.py:124-131,162`, patterns `PNB_CHQ_0..8` at `BankRegexConstants.py:140-148` (e.g. `PNB_CHQ_1 = "^TO TRF (.*)\\s?-\\s?[0-9]+$"`).
- **UCO** — patterns `UCO_CHQ_PATTERN1-4` (`BankRegexConstants.py:380-383`), used in `BankScripts/UCO.py`.
- **Bank of Maharashtra** — `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:169,175-179` (`^FRM (.*)`, `TRF TO/FOR ...`), plus cleanup at 213-214 using `CHQ_CLEAN`/`CHQ_CLEAN2` (`BankRegexConstants.py:361-362`).
- **CityUnion** — `BankScripts/CityUnion.py:130-133` (`FROM (.*)`, `BY TRF(.*)` on CHEQUE_DEPOSIT rows).
- **Indusind** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:178-183,190` (`^TRANSFER TO (.*)`, `TRF FROM (.*)`, etc.).
- **Axis** — `BankScripts/Axis.py:145,149-150` (`BRN-CLG-CHQ PAID TO (.*)`; pure-alpha description passthrough for cheque rows).
- **SBI** — `BankScripts/SBI.py:123` (`^CASH CHEQUE-|^CHEQUE DEPOSIT-|^CHEQUE WDL-` → `sep_by_dash(...,1,2)`).
- **IDBI** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:109` (description passthrough when remark holds cheque no.).
- **Kotak generic MICR patterns** — `CHQ_PATTERN1-4` at `BankRegexConstants.py:314-317` (`"MICR INWARD.*TO CLG (.*)"` etc.), plus bank-name stripper `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` at line 318.
- **FT-from-cheque hybrid patterns** — `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1-37` at `BankRegexConstants.py:263-299` (`"^TRF FROM CHQ [0-9]+ (.*)"` ...), consumed mainly by `Kotak.py` (~lines 175-230).

### 4c. NEFT credit name extraction

- **HDFC** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:157-162`:
  ```python
  [.str.contains("^NEFT [CD][Rr]-[A-z0-9]{11}-[0-9]{7,}-"), sep_by_dash(description,3,4)],
  [.str.contains("^NEFT [CD][Rr]-[A-z0-9]{11}-[A-Z]-"),    sep_by_dash(description,2,4)],
  [.str.contains("^IMPS-|^NEFT [CD][Rr]"),                 sep_by_dash(description,2,3)],
  [.str.contains("^NEFT\\s?/"),                            sep_by_(description,2,3)],
  [.str.contains("^00[0-9]+NEFT TO "),                     py_extract(description, "NEFT TO (.*)", 0)],
  ```
  NEFT categorization itself: `HDFC.py:60` (`"NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-|[0-9]NEFT TO|^BULK NEFT"`); junk-name reset at `HDFC.py:226`.
- **Kotak** — `BankScripts/Kotak.py:141-142,147-154` using `NEFT_PATTERN0-7` (`BankRegexConstants.py:206-213`, e.g. `NEFT_PATTERN0 = "^NEFT [0-9]+1DC (.*) [A-Z]{4}[0-9]"`); cleanup regex `NEFT_CLEAN_KOTAK` at line 214 strips IFSC-prefix bank codes.
- **Union Bank** — `BankScripts/UnionBank.py:81-92` using `UB_NEFT_1_UNION..8` (`BankRegexConstants.py:120-127`, e.g. `"^NEFT:IBUSER-(.*) SAA[0-9]+"`).
- **SBI** — `BankScripts/SBI.py:120-122` (`SBI_INB_7/8` from BankRegexConstants.py:49-50, then generic `sep_by_star(...,3,4)` with digit/punct strip for `transactionCategory == "NEFT"`); category rule at `SBI.py:55`.
- **ICICI** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:152,155,157-158` (`^NEFT-` → `sep_by_dash(...,2,3)`; `^INF/NEFT/` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`; generic NEFT/RTGS token picks); category rule at `ICICI.py:64`; refinement at `ICICI.py:228-229`.
- **Axis** — `BankScripts/Axis.py:126-130` (`^INB/NEFT/`, `^NEFT/MB`, `^NEFT/SK/`, `BRN-NEFT-` token positions).
- **Indusind** — stop-lists `NEFT_PAYMENT_STOP` / `NEFT_DEBIT_STOP` at `BankRegexConstants.py:333-334`.

### 4d. IMPS / instant-payment name extraction

- **Kotak** — `BankScripts/Kotak.py:109-116` with `IMPS_PATTERN1-8` (`BankRegexConstants.py:195-202`, e.g. `"^IMPS from (.*)Ref"`, `"IB IMPS TO (.*) Ref"`), and `Kotak.py:243-247` with `RCVD_FROM_IMPS1-5` (`BankRegexConstants.py:234-238`, `"^Received from (.*) IMPS REF"`).
- **SBI** — `BankScripts/SBI.py:149-152` using `SBI_IMPS_1-3` (`BankRegexConstants.py:60-62`); junk cleanup at `SBI.py:174-176,185`.
- **ICICI** — `BankScripts/ICICI.py:62` (`^MMT/IMPS` → category IMPS); extraction `ICICI.py:163-165` (slash-token position 3/4 depending on count); heavy refinement `ICICI.py:195-205,216,228,231-232`.
- **HDFC** — `BankScripts/HDFC.py:59` (category), `155-156,159` (Razorpay IMPS token picks; generic `sep_by_dash(...,2,3)`), `231-232` (pasfar/razorpay reruns), `251` (`^IMPS.*-UNREGISTERED-` → token 4/5).
- **Axis** — `BankScripts/Axis.py:119-123` (`IMPS/P2A.*RAZORPAY` → token 5/6; `IMPS/P2A/[0-9]+/[0-9]+/[A-Z]` → token 4/5; UPI/IMPS/IFT → token 3/4).
- **IDFC** — `BankScripts/IDFC.py:71-72` (`IMPS-INET/`, `IMPS-MOB/` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`, skipped for ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION rows).
- Kotak mobile-banking strings: `STOP_STRINGS` at `BankRegexConstants.py:191` (`"^RECEIVED FROM |^Sent to |...IMPS|SENT MONEY TO"`).

### 4e. Small verification-deposit ("penny drop") detection → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`

Pattern is always *(narration matches verification regex)* AND *(amount is ±1 or < 2)*:

| File:Line | Rule |
|---|---|
| `BankScripts/HDFC.py:13` | `BANK_VER` regex & `amount.lt(2)` |
| `BankScripts/ICICI.py:11` | `BANK_VER_ICICI` & `amount.isin([1,-1])` & not `RVSL` |
| `BankScripts/SBI.py:12` | `ACC_VERIF` & CREDIT & `amount.eq(1)` |
| `BankScripts/Axis.py:24-26` | `BANK_VER` & ±1; amount==1 & "MANDATE"; **any** CREDIT of exactly 1 |
| `BankScripts/Kotak.py:13-14` | `Karz Xx4002` or `^Received from [A-Z]` & CREDIT & amount==1 |
| `BankScripts/Paytm.py:15-16` | `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` (`"Acc? Validation By Me"`); `IMPS` & amount==1 & CREDIT |
| `BankScripts/Indusind.py:29-31` | `BANK_VER` & ±1; amount==1 & MANDATE; amount "1" & DEBIT |
| `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py:36-37` | `BANK_VER` & ±1; any CREDIT of "1" |
| `BankScripts/Canara.py:19` | `BANK_VERIF` & `amount.lt(1)` |
| `BankScripts/RBL.py:15` | `ACC_VERI_RBL` & `amount.lt(2)` |
| Others (all `amount.isin([1,-1])` or `.eq(1)`) | BOB.py:12, BOI.py:12, IDBI.py:12, IDFC.py:12, Karnataka.py:12, UnionBank.py:12, Syndicate.py:12, Central.py:12, Andhra.py:12, PNB.py:12 (`lt(2)`), YES.py:14, SouthIndian.py:12, StandardCharted.py:13, TamilnadMerchantile.py:13, AuSmallFinanceBank.py:12 |

Verification regex constants live in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`: `ACC_VERIF` (line 6), `BANK_VER_ICICI` (69), `BANK_VER_HD` (75), `BANK_VER_BOI` (110), `ACC_VERI_UNION` (116), `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` (133), `ACC_VERI_SYNDICATE` (163), `BANK_VERIF` (321), `BANK_VER` (327 — shared by Axis/HDFC/BOM/Indusind), `ACC_VERI_ANDHRA` (365), `ACC_VERI_YES` (396), `ACC_VERI_RBL` (410), `ACC_VERI_CB` (415), `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` (428), `ACC_VERI_SCB` (431). Typical content: `"verif|nydrop|valida|GOOGLE.*TEMPOR|Accountv|bankAccountV|Authenticat|...|PennyD|bankAc|Accoun"`.

Downstream: `Purpose.py:165` re-flags 1-rupee LOAN rows as ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION; `SalaryDetection.py:205` and `Paytm.py:96` blank names/categories for verification rows.

### Key takeaway
This is a pure rules-engine microservice: ~5,300 lines of per-bank pandas regex rules plus ~4,000 lines of shared regex/merchant dictionaries, exposed via one Flask endpoint, with **no committed tests or labelled corpus** (fixtures were `.gitignore`d as `*.csv`). Any test harness would have to be created from scratch, most naturally by calling `categorize_<Bank>_transactions()` directly with synthetic DataFrames containing `description`, `type`, `amount`, `remark`, `balanceAfterTransaction` columns.

import sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import pandas as pd, numpy as np

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.PNB import categorize_PNB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Canara import categorize_Canara_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.AuSmallFinanceBank import categorize_AuSmallFinance_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Kotak import categorize_Kotak_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.SBI import categorize_SBI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Axis import categorize_Axis_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.UnionBank import categorize_UnionBank_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.StandardCharted import categorize_SCB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Central import categorize_Central_transactions

def run(fn, rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ["description","type","remark"]:
        if col not in df: df[col] = ""
    if "amount" not in df: df["amount"] = 100.0
    if "balanceAfterTransaction" not in df: df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 1000.0
    df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df["amount"])
    out = fn(df.copy(), accountType)
    return out[["description","remark","type","amount","transactionCategory","partyName"]]

pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 60)

print("=== F-1: bare cheque-number remark, DEBIT ===")
print("PNB:")
print(run(categorize_PNB_transactions, [
    {"description":"", "remark":"123456", "type":"DEBIT", "amount":5000},
    {"description":"", "remark":"12345",  "type":"DEBIT", "amount":5000},
    {"description":"", "remark":"123456", "type":"CREDIT","amount":5000},
]))

print()
print("=== F-2: CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-<NAME> ===")
for name, fn in [("Canara",categorize_Canara_transactions),
                 ("AuSmallFinance",categorize_AuSmallFinance_transactions),
                 ("Central",categorize_Central_transactions),
                 ("HDFC",categorize_HDFC_transactions)]:
    print(name)
    print(run(fn, [
        {"description":"CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR", "type":"DEBIT", "amount":5000},
    ]))

print()
print("=== F-5: penny-drop credit ===")
print("Canara:")
print(run(categorize_Canara_transactions, [
    {"description":"NEFT PENNYDROP VERIF", "type":"CREDIT", "amount":1},
    {"description":"NEFT PENNYDROP VERIF", "type":"CREDIT", "amount":0.5},
]))

def run(fn, descs, typ="CREDIT"):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"description":descs})
    df["type"]=typ; df["remark"]=""; df["amount"]=4999.0; df["balanceAfterTransaction"]=10000.0
    out = fn(df, "SAVING")
    for _,r in out.iterrows():
        print(f"   {r.description[:58]:60s} -> [{r.transactionCategory:16s}] party={r.partyName!r}")

print("Canara IMPS credit layouts:")
run(canara, [

import warnings; warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Syndicate import categorize_Syndicate_transactions

def full(fn, bank, rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ["description","type","remark"]:
        if col not in df: df[col]=""
    df["amount"]=pd.to_numeric(df.get("amount",100.0)); df["balanceAfterTransaction"]=10000.0
    t = fn(df, accountType)

    r = salary_detection(t)
    t = t if r is None else r
    for _,x in t.iterrows():
        print(f"  {bank:10s} {x.description[:45]:47s} rem={x.remark!r:10s} [{x.transactionCategory:20s}] party={x.partyName!r}")

  {"description":"NEFT:N123456789012345:RAVI KUMAR","type":"CREDIT","amount":9000},
])
print("F-5 Canara penny-drop credit:")
full(categorize_Canara_transactions, "CANARA", [

steps.message:
All five findings are resolved. Since the repo ships no fixtures or tests, I located each defect by cross-checking every rule against its sibling rules (the same layout handled elsewhere in the same or a peer bank script), then verified empirically by running the actual categorizers before/after on a 35-bank × 49-narration sweep.

## Root causes and fixes

**F-1 — bare cheque-number debit → TRANSFER** (`BankScripts/PNB.py:60`)
The DEBIT remark rule accepted only 5-digit numbers (`^[0-9]{5}$`) while its CREDIT twin on the very next line accepts `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. A 6-digit bare cheque number on a debit matched nothing and fell to the TRANSFER default. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$` — a strict superset, so every currently-matching row is untouched.

**F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty "Micr Clg"** (`Canara.py:164-165`, `AuSmallFinanceBank.py:78`)
The generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule takes dash-token 1, which for this layout is the clearing tag. Canara's own neighbouring rule (`Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` → token 2) and Central Bank's handling of the identical layout show the name lives at token 2 when a clearing tag is present. Added the `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` alternative to the tag-aware token-2 rule (and an equivalent guard rule in AU Small Finance, which shares the layout). Only narrations literally containing `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` change.

**F-3 — plain NEFT credit name blank** (`YES.py:103`)
`^NEFT\s?-N[0-9]` (the standard `NEFT-N<15-digit UTR>-<NAME>` layout) was lumped into the token-3 rule meant for `NET-NEFT-…`; on the 3-token layout, token 3 doesn't exist → blank. It also made rule 109 (`^NEFT-[A-Z0-9]{16}-` → token 2, i.e. exactly this layout) unreachable dead code — the tell. Split the rule: `NET-NEFT-`/`NEFT -RETURN` keep token 3; the N-UTR variants now take token 2.

**F-4 — inbound IMPS credit shows the reference number** (`Syndicate.py:69`)
`^IMPS:` took colon-token 1 — the 12-digit reference — while the identically shaped `^NEFT:`/`^RTGS:` narrations two lines below correctly take token 2, and Syndicate has no numeric-junk cleanup, so the raw number surfaced. Changed to `sep_by_colon(…,2,3)`.

**F-5 — ₹1 penny-drop credit → TRANSFER** (`Canara.py:19`)
The verification rule used `amount.lt(1)`, excluding the ₹1 confirmation credit itself. Every other bank uses `eq(1)`, `isin([1,-1])` or `lt(2)`. Changed to `lt(2)` — again a superset, so sub-rupee rows that already matched are unmoved (using `eq(1)` instead would have shifted them).

## Regression containment

- Snapshotted the full output (category + counterparty) of all 35 bank categorizers over a 49-narration corpus (cheques, penny drops, NEFT/IMPS/RTGS/UPI layouts, POS, ATM, salary, charges) before and after. The diff contains **only** the rows corresponding to the five listed forms — no currently-correct row changes value.
- Re-ran the fixed rows through the downstream `purpose()` → `clean_names()` stages to confirm the restored names/categories survive the full enrichment path (`Ravi Kumar` / `CHEQUE_PAID` / `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` etc.).
- All 35 bank scripts still compile and execute cleanly.

Net change: 7 lines across 5 bank scripts (`git diff --stat` above). Nothing committed — let me know if you'd like a commit prepared.
